Operations handbook: cold-chain receiving. This handbook describes how the receiving team checks temperature-controlled deliveries at the north dock. Every pallet is logged against its delivery note before it leaves the vehicle, and any pallet that arrives outside the agreed band is held in the quarantine bay until the quality lead has reviewed the data logger file. The aim is simple: no product should reach the chilled store without a recorded temperature history that matches the supplier's certificate. Start each shift by confirming that the handheld thermometer has been calibrated within the last thirty days. The calibration label sits on the back of the device, and the date is also written in the shift log. If the label is missing or out of date, use the reference thermometer kept in the supervisor's office, and record the change of device on the first line of the log. When a vehicle arrives, check the seal number against the consignment note before the doors are opened. A broken or mismatched seal is recorded with a photograph, and the driver signs the exception form. Measure the core temperature of at least three cases per pallet, chosen from the top, middle and bottom layers. Frozen goods must read at or below minus eighteen degrees, and chilled goods must read between zero and five degrees unless the product specification says otherwise. Write each reading in the log with the time, the case reference and the initials of the person who took it. Once the load has been accepted, move it to the correct storage zone within forty minutes. Stock that waits longer on the dock is recorded as a deviation, and the shift supervisor must explain the delay in the end-of-shift report. Labels must show the receiving date, the best-before date and the lot number, and they must face outwards. Damaged packaging is treated differently from temperature deviations. A dented case with an intact product seal can be accepted with a note, while a case with a split seal or visible leakage is rejected and returned on the same vehicle. Each month the team reviews the logger files from a sample of deliveries and compares them with the handheld readings. Differences larger than one degree are investigated, and the findings are summarised for the operations board.

Meeting minutes: capacity planning, third quarter. Attendees were the operations lead, the two shift supervisors, the finance partner and the procurement manager. The first item reviewed the utilisation of the packing line over the summer. Average utilisation was seventy-one per cent, with the lowest figures in the second week of July when two operators were on leave. The team agreed to cross-train three people from the returns desk so that the line can be staffed without overtime during the holiday weeks. The second item covered the pallet storage plan for the new warehouse bay. The layout drawing was approved with one change: the fast-moving lines move to the aisle nearest the dock doors. Finance asked for a monthly forecast of storage costs, broken down by zone, before the next budget round. The procurement manager will supply the supplier rate cards by the end of the month. The third item was the schedule for the annual maintenance of the conveyors. Two stops are planned, both on Sundays, and the production planner will move the affected orders to the weekday shifts. Action owners were confirmed for each point. The next meeting is on the second Tuesday of October, in the room on the second floor, and the agenda will be circulated three days before.

Product guide: the compact ventilation unit. The compact ventilation unit is designed for small kitchens, storerooms and workshops where a full duct system is not practical. It moves up to two hundred and eighty cubic metres of air per hour on its highest setting and runs quietly on the lowest. Installation takes about an hour. Choose a wall with a clear run to the outside, mark the position of the mounting plate, and drill the holes at the marked points. Use the rubber gasket supplied with the unit to seal the gap between the housing and the wall, because a poor seal lets cold air return into the room. Connect the unit to a dedicated circuit protected by a residual-current device. The wiring diagram on the inside of the cover shows the colour code for each conductor. The filter should be cleaned every four weeks in a kitchen with heavy use, and every twelve weeks in a storeroom. Wash the filter in warm water with a mild detergent, let it dry completely, and refit it with the arrow pointing towards the fan. The fan blades should be checked for dust during each cleaning. A light brush is enough; avoid water on the motor housing. If the unit makes a rattling noise, check that the mounting screws are tight and that the grille is not touching the blade. The warranty covers manufacturing faults for two years from the date of purchase. Keep the receipt with the guide.

Travel notes: a week in the Lofoten islands. The first day is best spent in Svolvær, where the harbour has good coffee and a small museum about the fishing history of the region. From there, the road to Henningsvær runs along the coast, with viewpoints that are worth a short stop, especially in the evening light. Book the ferry crossings a few days ahead in the summer, because the morning sailings fill quickly and the next departure can be several hours later. The hiking trails near Reine are well marked. The climb to the lookout takes about ninety minutes return, and sturdy shoes are needed on the wet rock near the top. Bring layers. The weather changes quickly over the sea, and a warm jacket is useful even on a sunny afternoon. Most small restaurants close early in the shoulder season, so plan dinner before four in the afternoon if you are travelling in September. The local bakeries are open early and sell cinnamon buns that are worth the walk. Fuel stations are few on the outer islands. Fill the tank whenever you pass a station with a full pump, even if the gauge still shows half. On the last day, drive slowly through the tunnels, keep an eye out for pedestrians, and leave time to return the rental car before the office closes.

Changelog for the scheduling module, versions 4.2 to 4.7. Version 4.7 adds a day view for shared rooms, so that a planner can see every booking for a room on one screen. The room list can now be filtered by floor and by capacity, and the filter choice is remembered for the next visit. Version 4.6 fixed a problem where recurring meetings that crossed a daylight saving change were shown one hour early. Recurring events now keep their local start time, and the series editor warns before it changes the time of a single occurrence. Version 4.5 introduced the reminder setting for each calendar. Reminders are sent by email and can be set to fifteen minutes, one hour or one day before the event. Version 4.4 improved the speed of the monthly view on large calendars by loading only the visible weeks. Version 4.3 changed the export format for attendee lists to include the department and the cost centre. Older exports still open in the same way. Version 4.2 removed the deprecated bulk-import screen. Use the spreadsheet template on the help page instead, which accepts the same columns.
